title: UPSTYLE_Backdoor_Investigation_b2f
description: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on one of its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor named UPSTYLE. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on one of its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor named UPSTYLE. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this case is `update.py.service`. The flag type is the service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the attacker.
levels.solution: To determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after a system reboot, you can use the `systemctl status update.py.service` command to check the status of the service. The output will show you the unit file that is used to start the service automatically. In this case, the service is started using a systemd service unit file. The flag type is the path to the systemd service unit file.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd configuration files to find how the service is set to start automatically.

levels.title: Suspicious File Discovery
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious service. This will help you gather more information about the malware and its behavior.
levels.solution: To locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl cat update.py.service` command to view the contents of the service unit file. The unit file will show you the path to the executable. In this case, the executable is located at `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`. The flag type is the path to the executable.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the service unit file to find the path to the executable.
